problems.stem: You have a 30-minute revision sprint. Your budget sheet shows a #REF! error in the Total cell, and the page also has a plain default font. Which do you fix first and why?
options: The font, because it is the first thing people see.
The #REF! error, because a wrong or broken total fails the artifact no matter how it looks; cosmetics come after correctness.
Neither; 30 minutes is too short to fix anything.
Both at once by restarting the file.
problems.explanation: Triage by impact. A broken total is a correctness failure; fix it before any cosmetic change in a limited time box.

problems.stem: During the sprint you make six edits to your spreadsheet, then overwrite the file each time with no record. A peer asks what you changed. Why is this a problem?
options: It is not a problem; the final file speaks for itself.
Without a changelog you cannot show what changed or revert an edit that broke something, so the sprint is not reviewable.
Six edits is too many for one sprint.
You should have used a different spreadsheet program.
problems.explanation: A short changelog of time, change, and reason makes the sprint traceable and lets you roll back a change that made things worse.

problems.stem: With 20 minutes left in the sprint, an AI tool suggests rebuilding your whole HTML layout with a CSS grid. You have three small known bugs. What is the disciplined move?
options: Start the full grid rebuild; the AI knows best.
Decline the rebuild for now, fix the three known bugs within the time box, and log the grid idea as a future item.
Ignore the AI entirely and stop working.
Rebuild half the layout and leave it unfinished.
problems.explanation: A sprint revises, it does not rebuild. Use the time for high-impact targeted fixes and defer larger rework so you do not ship something broken.

problems.stem: Which changelog entry best documents a sprint edit so a reviewer can trace it?
options: '14:05 - replaced #REF! in Total (B14) with =SUM(B2:B13)=8,420; verified against the receipts tab. Reason: broken reference after a deleted row.'
'Worked on the file for a while.'
problems.explanation: A traceable entry gives the time, the exact cell and formula, the verified result, and the reason, so a reviewer can confirm the fix.
